# Phrase arm scores executed outcomes for the write tasks

- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; benchmark arm change)
- **Milestone:** Measure first: does Phrase beat plain C# on tokens and attempts at an equal or better pass rate?
- **Source:** Decider D66 (2026-10-27), splitting card 088 into thin slices: the C# arm scores executed outcomes (D37) and the emitter now compiles orders.phrase end to end (cards 039 to 087), so the Phrase arm must score the same executed outcomes before any head-to-head. The frozen bar is Decider D32 and is not changed by this card.
- **Depends on:** 087, 097
- **Story:** As Riley, I want the Phrase arm to compile a model's Phrase reply with the C# adapter and run the write tasks' outcome cases against the generated code, so that a Phrase pass means the same executed behaviour as a plain C# pass.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given tasks 001 and 002 and a fake model whose recorded reply is a correct Phrase module, When the Phrase arm runs them, Then the row has proof level specs-passed, patched false, scored executed outcomes, and passes; a wrong reply fails and the row names the failing outcome case
  2. Given each task folder, When the suite is checked, Then it holds an outcomes.json byte-identical to the C# twin's (a failing check names the task whose copy drifted)
  3. Given the existing parse-resolve rows and the default run, When this card is merged, Then old rows still read as parse-resolve and a run without the new option keeps its prompt hash and launch arguments

## Context

- Same-level rule (Decider D37): Phrase and plain C# rows are compared only at the specs-passed proof level. The Phrase arm compiles the model's Phrase module with the C# adapter (Phrase.Adapters.CSharp), builds the generated projects, and runs the task's outcome cases against the generated phrase methods by reflection, exactly as tools/Phrase.BenchCs runs them against model code, plus the model's own generated specs must pass.
- The single source of a task's outcome cases is the C# twin's outcomes.json under bench/csharp-baseline/tasks/<id>/; the Phrase task folder gets a copy (a test asserts the two files are byte-identical so they cannot drift). The model only writes Phrase, so no row can be green by editing generated C#: the row records patched false by construction.
- Fixed head-to-head development tasks: 001, 002, 004, 005, 007, 008, 010, 011 (the eight with C# twins). Tasks 003, 006, 009 and 012 stay Phrase-only and are not compared. Fix tasks 010 and 011 keep their BROKEN start fixtures (PH330 on the phrase trigger; the Text/Int mismatch): only the reference solution compiles.
- Safety rules apply in full. Existing result rows keep their proof level; old parse-resolve rows are never mixed with specs-passed rows. Tests use fake model commands (no real model); a correct recorded reply passes and a wrong reply fails naming the failing outcome.
- Smallest scope: the write tasks (001 write-greeting returns Text, 002 write-total returns Int) and the outcome runner (generated Api assembly plus a harness test project, built in a fresh directory per attempt like the C# arm). Read, modify and fix tasks are cards 099 and 100.
